catalog_quote: Japhug has no tonal contrasts. However, there is morphologically determined stress. Phonological words only have one stress, which is located by default on the final syllable of the word (§3.8.1, §11.6.1). The personal agreement suffixes (§14.2.1, §11.3) and the peg suffix -ci (§11.4) never receive stress, and their vowels are optionally devoiced. ... Stress can be antepenultimate in the case of verb forms with two suffixes as in to-k-ɤmɯ-rpú-ndʑi-ci ‘they bumped into each other’ (ifr-peg-recip-bump-du-peg). There are only three verbal prefixes which can attract stress: the inverse -wɣ- (§14.3.2.7), the negative Sensory mɯ́j- (§13.1.1, §21.3.2.1), and the interrogative ɯ- (§21.7.4.1). new_statements.quote: Unlike other Rgyalrong languages (Sun 2005, Lin 2012), Japhug has no tonal contrasts. However, there is morphologically determined stress. Phonological words only have one stress, which is located by default on the final syllable of the word (regardless of its part of speech). The personal agreement suffixes and the evidential suffix /-ci/ never receive stress, and their vowels are optionally devoiced. For instance, /tɤ-ndza-t-a/ 'I ate it' (PFV-eat-PST-1SG) is realized as [tɤndzátḁ] or [tɤndzáta]. In verbal forms with these prefixes, stress is penultimate, or even antepenultimate in the case of verb forms with two suffixes

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog carries Japhug with an empty rule and no existing stress statements; this source supplies the missing placement (default word-final, one stress per phonological word, no tone) together with the morphological exceptions, so it fills rather than contradicts the record.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Japhug is not tonal. Each phonological word carries a single stress, by default on the last syllable regardless of word class; the author calls it 'morphologically determined' because a closed set of affixes shifts it: person-agreement suffixes and the evidential -ci are never stressed (so such verb forms are stressed on the penult or antepenult), while the inverse prefix -wɣ-, the negative testimonial mɯ́j- and the comitative-adverb prefix kɤ́- attract the stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; the source states that phonological words have only one stress.
new_statements.exceptions: (1) Personal agreement suffixes and the evidential suffix /-ci/ never receive stress and their vowels are optionally devoiced, giving penultimate stress, or antepenultimate with two suffixes, e.g. /to-k-ɤmɯ-rpú-ndʑɯ-ci/ 'they bumped into each other' (p. 446). (2) p. 447: 'Only two verbal prefixes, the inverse /-wɣ-/ and the negative testimonial /mɯ́j-/, attract stress, as in /pɯ-tɯ́-wɣ-mto/ "he saw you" and /mɯ́j-ndze/ "he does not eat it".' (3) p. 447: comitative adverbs ('together with X') are built with 'the stress-bearing /kɤ́-/ prefix with a reduplicated noun stem', e.g. /kɤ́-jwɯ~jwaʁ/ 'with its leaves' (Table 18). (4) p. 445: unaccented clitics such as the linker /nɤ/ 'if' are outside the stress domain; /e/ 'only occurs in the last (accented) syllable of a word'.
new_statements.identity_note: Jacques 2019 describes the Japhug of Kamnyu village (/kɤmɲɯ/, Ganmuniao) in Gdongbrgyad area (/ʁdɯrɟɤt/, Longerjia), Mbarkhams county, Rngaba prefecture, Sichuan; the data come from one speaker, Tshendzin (female, b. 1950). The 2004 thesis mentions in passing that the gSar-rdzong variety of Japhug has the stressed negative prefix as mɛ́j-, i.e. a segmental (not accentual) dialect difference. No other variety is claimed to differ in stress placement.

audit.reasoning: The classification (morphological stress: one stress per phonological word, default final / verb-stem-final, indexation suffixes and -ci never stressed, three stress-attracting prefixes, comitative kɤ́-) rests on the definitive open-access reference grammar (Jacques 2025, 2nd ed., LangSci, ~1,600 pp) and the deciding quotations are verbatim at the stated pages (p. 68/PDF 102, pp. 68-69/PDF 102-103, p. 480/PDF 514). Two further primary sources by the same author, downloaded now from open repositories (2004 Paris VII thesis pp. 203/343/401; 2019 JIPA Illustration pp. 446-447), give the same account; the only difference is that JIPA lists two stress-attracting prefixes and the grammar three (interrogative ɯ- added), which the record already follows.
